Chapter 7: Navigating Seasons of Dryness and Doubt
Let’s be honest—no matter how consistent you are in your spiritual practices, there’ll be times when God just feels distant... or even silent. You know those stretches where nothing seems to click? It’s easy to wonder if you’re doing something wrong, or if the connection was ever real to begin with.
But here’s some reassurance: these dry spells are a normal part of any spiritual journey. They aren’t a sign you’ve failed. In fact, they can be an invitation—a chance to grow in new ways. Think about it. Every relationship has phases, right? There are times of deep closeness, and then there are times when you drift apart a little. The same thing happens in your relationship with God.
So how do you navigate these seasons of dryness? There are a few principles that really help.
First, just acknowledge those feelings of distance or doubt. Don’t beat yourself up over them. It’s okay to feel lost sometimes.
Second, try to stick with your simple daily practices—even if they feel empty or routine. Sometimes, just showing up is what matters most.
And third, reach out to people you trust. Maybe it’s a friend, a mentor, or your spiritual community. You don’t have to walk through this alone.
Instead of pulling away, try bringing your questions and frustrations right into the conversation with God. Sometimes the most real, honest prayer you can offer sounds like, “I feel far away,” or, “I’m not sure if you’re even listening right now.” That kind of vulnerability? It can actually open the door to new understanding—or comfort you never expected.
And here’s something to keep in mind: even when it feels like nothing’s happening, growth is often taking place below the surface. Think about seeds planted in winter. You don’t see much at first, but roots are growing deeper, quietly preparing for what’s next.
If you look back, you’ll probably notice that these dry seasons often build resilience, empathy, and clarity. Maybe you’ve seen it in others, too—a parent who keeps praying for their child year after year, even with no response, or someone who just keeps showing up for quiet reflection, even when it feels pointless. Over time, these small acts of faithfulness can bear fruit in the most unexpected ways.
So, what’s the key? Trust the process, and give yourself permission to hold both struggle and hope at the same time. Dryness and doubt aren’t the end of the road—they’re actually part of the ongoing invitation to grow, to deepen, and to discover a relationship that goes even further than you imagined.
